summary: Points to three annotated templates for documents that define MIB modules. They aim to reduce editors' work and make these documents more uniform and easier to review. It is a Best Current Practice.

eli5.summary: This is a set of fill-in forms for people writing network management documents, so the documents all look alike.

questions: template for internet drafts with mib modules
subtitle: Three ready-made templates that help authors write Internet-Drafts containing MIB modules.

tldr.problem: Editors of documents that define MIB modules often copied older documents as a starting point, but boilerplates and required elements change over time.
tldr.mechanism: The MIB Doctors directorate produced three annotated templates, kept on the IETF Tools web site and updated occasionally to match current requirements.
tldr.outcome: Documents become more uniform and easier to read and review, which speeds publication.

today: RFC 5249 is a Best Current Practice published in July 2008. No later RFC is recorded as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Why Templates
sections.content:
RFC 5249 references three annotated templates for IETF documents that contain the definition of MIB modules. They are meant to reduce the work of editors, make such documents more uniform and easier to read and review, and so improve their quality and speed up their publication.

It had been common practice to reuse an existing MIB module document as a template. The RFC says this has problems because boilerplates and other required elements change over time. The referenced templates are instead made available on the IETF Tools web site and occasionally updated.
sections.eli5: Copying an old homework sheet is risky because the rules change. A fresh, up-to-date form is safer.

sections.title: The Three Templates
sections.content:
The MIB Doctors directorate produced three templates aimed at Internet-Drafts containing MIB modules. The first is an XML template for editors who use XML2RFC, with advice echoing guidelines from RFC 4181 embedded in comments. The second is a text template with advice embedded in the document. The third is a plain text template with no advice.

The templates contain the boilerplates required for IETF MIB module documents, and sections that describe the purpose and organization of the MIB module and its relationship to other MIB modules. This helps a MIB Doctor understand the module and speeds review. There are a number of MUSTs in the templates, especially in the advice; these usually refer to IESG requirements for Internet-Drafts.
sections.eli5: There are three forms: one with tips for a certain writing tool, one with tips in plain text, and one with no tips at all.

sections.title: What Is Not Included
sections.content:
The templates do not include a template for the MIB module itself. Tools that validate MIB modules typically need the module separated from the surrounding document. The MIB Doctors therefore suggest developing the module outside the document and then including it in the text written with the templates.

Editors should also read RFC 4181, which describes best current practices for MIB module document editing. On security, the memo has no direct impact on network security, though the templates include boilerplate and advice for the Security Considerations section.
sections.eli5: The forms cover the words around the main part, not the main part itself. You write that part separately and slot it in.

references.text: Heard, C., "Guidelines for Authors and Reviewers of MIB Documents", BCP 111, RFC 4181, September 2005.
